# Definitions and Symbols

R<sup>2</sup>D uses familiar mathematical words in deliberately specific
ways.

In particular:

- a **boundary** defines a count domain;
- a **macrostate** is a readable state at that boundary;
- a **microstate** is one compatible joint realization of immediately
  subordinate boundaries;
- **multiplicity**, **occurrence**, and **occupancy** are different kinds of
  count;
- **possibility** is not probability;
- **recurrence** is not occurrence;
- **closure** is not automatically reversibility;
- and primitive R<sup>2</sup>D quantities are dimensionless before physical
  mappings are assigned.

This page is a reference.

For the conceptual development, begin with
[Counting Requires Distinguishability →](counting.qmd).

## The Most Important Rule

Every R<sup>2</sup>D quantity must be interpreted relative to the boundary at
which it is defined.

Thus:

> **Always ask: At which boundary is this quantity readable?**

The same physical realization can have different count meanings at adjacent
boundaries.

That boundary index is part of the definition.

# Boundary and Index Notation

## \(B_n\) — Count boundary

$$
\boxed{
B_n
}
$$

is the count boundary at recursive level \(n\).

A boundary is not necessarily a physical surface.

It defines:

- the count domain;
- the readable distinctions;
- which subordinate realizations are compatible;
- how those realizations are classified into macrostates;
- and which completed local realizations belong to enclosing occurrences.

[Boundaries Define Scientific Objects →](boundaries.qmd)

## \(n\) — Recursive boundary level

The index

$$
n
$$

labels a recursive boundary level.

Adjacent levels are written

$$
B_{n-1},
\qquad
B_n,
\qquad
B_{n+1}.
$$

The index does not primitively mean spatial size, physical length, or elapsed
time.

It specifies position in the recursive count hierarchy.

## \(B_{n-1,\alpha}\) — Subordinate peer boundary

Immediately subordinate peer boundaries are written

$$
\boxed{
B_{n-1,\alpha}
}
$$

where

$$
\alpha\in I_{n-1}.
$$

The index \(\alpha\) distinguishes ordinary peer boundaries at the same
recursive level.

A second peer may be labeled \(\beta\).

## \(I_n\) — Peer index set

$$
\boxed{
I_n
}
$$

is the set indexing peer boundaries at recursive level \(n\).

## \(i,j,k\) — Macrostate labels

Letters such as

$$
i,\ j,\ k
$$

label readable macrostates within one boundary-defined state domain.

For example,

$$
i\rightarrow k
$$

denotes a readable macrostate transition.

## \(H,L\) — Opposed closure legs

For a minimal two-leg closure,

$$
H
$$

and

$$
L
$$

label the two opposed oriented paths.

They should not be confused with recursive boundary indices.

## \((r)\) — One realized occurrence

A superscript

$$
(r)
$$

labels one realized occurrence.

For example,

$$
\mu_n^{(r)}
$$

is one realized formal microstate.

It is not a boundary index.

## \(\Delta\) — Oriented difference

$$
\Delta
$$

denotes an oriented difference between states or an accumulated oriented
difference along a path.

For example,

$$
\Delta S_{n,i\rightarrow k}
=
S_{n,k}-S_{n,i}.
$$

Reversing the orientation reverses the sign when the underlying coordinate is
state defined.

## \(\delta_{\mathcal C}\) — Increment associated with one closure

$$
\delta_{\mathcal C}
$$

denotes an increment associated with one specified realized closure.

It is used especially for the enclosing background increment.

# State Domains

## \(\mathfrak X_{n-1,\alpha}\) — Peer realization domain

For subordinate peer

$$
B_{n-1,\alpha},
$$

let

$$
\boxed{
\mathfrak X_{n-1,\alpha}
}
$$

denote its possible realization domain.

## Joint subordinate realization space

The unrestricted joint realization space subordinate to \(B_n\) is

$$
\boxed{
\prod_{\alpha\in I_{n-1}}
\mathfrak X_{n-1,\alpha}.
}
$$

This contains all formally possible combinations of subordinate peer
realizations.

The enclosing boundary need not admit all of them.

## \(\mathfrak M_n\) — Formal microstate domain

The compatible subset is

$$
\boxed{
\mathfrak M_n
\subseteq
\prod_{\alpha\in I_{n-1}}
\mathfrak X_{n-1,\alpha}.
}
$$

This is the formal microstate domain at \(B_n\).

Compatibility is defined by the boundary of the whole.

## \(\mu_n\) — Formal microstate

One formal microstate is

$$
\boxed{
\mu_n
\in
\mathfrak M_n.
}
$$

A formal microstate is one compatible joint realization of the immediately
subordinate peers.

It is not simply "the smallest physical state."

Microstate is a relation to a boundary.

## \(\mathcal M_n\) — Readable macrostate set

$$
\boxed{
\mathcal M_n
}
$$

is the set of macrostates readable at \(B_n\).

A macrostate is therefore a distinguishable state relative to that boundary.

## \(i\in\mathcal M_n\) — One readable macrostate

$$
\boxed{
i\in\mathcal M_n
}
$$

denotes one readable macrostate.

## \(\pi_n\) — Macrostate classification map

The boundary classifies compatible formal microstates by

$$
\boxed{
\pi_n:
\mathfrak M_n
\rightarrow
\mathcal M_n.
}
$$

If

$$
\pi_n(\mu_n)=i,
$$

then formal microstate \(\mu_n\) is classified as macrostate \(i\).

## \(\pi_n^{-1}(i)\) — Macrostate fiber

The preimage

$$
\boxed{
\pi_n^{-1}(i)
}
$$

is the set of formal microstates classified as macrostate \(i\).

This set is sometimes called the **fiber** over \(i\).

The vertical bars

$$
\left|\pi_n^{-1}(i)\right|
$$

mean the cardinality—the number of members—of that set.

[Macrostate and Microstate →](macrostate-microstate.qmd)

# Multiplicity

## \(W_{n,i}\) — Native multiplicity

The native multiplicity of macrostate \(i\) is

$$
\boxed{
W_{n,i}
=
\left|
\pi_n^{-1}(i)
\right|.
}
$$

It counts how many compatible formal microstates belong to macrostate \(i\).

Multiplicity is **possible count**.

It is not occurrence count.

It is not occupancy.

## \(S_{n,i}\) — Logarithmic multiplicity

Define

$$
\boxed{
S_{n,i}
=
\ln W_{n,i}.
}
$$

In primitive R<sup>2</sup>D,

$$
S
$$

is a dimensionless logarithmic possible-count coordinate.

It is not yet thermodynamic entropy in units of energy per temperature.

## \(\Delta S_{n,i\rightarrow k}\) — Native multiplicity difference

For

$$
i\rightarrow k,
$$

$$
\boxed{
\Delta S_{n,i\rightarrow k}
=
S_{n,k}-S_{n,i}
=
\ln
\left(
\frac{W_{n,k}}{W_{n,i}}
\right).
}
$$

## \(\Theta_n\) — Total boundary multiplicity

The total possible multiplicity of the boundary is

$$
\boxed{
\Theta_n
=
|\mathfrak M_n|
=
\sum_{i\in\mathcal M_n}
W_{n,i}.
}
$$

## \(S_n^{\mathrm{tot}}\) — Total logarithmic multiplicity

$$
\boxed{
S_n^{\mathrm{tot}}
=
\ln\Theta_n.
}
$$

## \(\mathcal W_n\) — Native multiplicity landscape

$$
\boxed{
\mathcal W_n
=
\{W_{n,i}\}_{i\in\mathcal M_n}.
}
$$

## \(\mathcal S_n\) — Native logarithmic multiplicity landscape

$$
\boxed{
\mathcal S_n
=
\{S_{n,i}\}_{i\in\mathcal M_n}.
}
$$

The native landscape remains fixed while the boundary definition and
classification remain fixed.

A particular realization does not create it.

[Multiplicity →](multiplicity.qmd)

# The Two Primitive Count Operations

For compatible possibilities,

$$
\boxed{
W_{\mathrm{joint}}
=
\prod_\alpha W_\alpha.
}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\boxed{
\ln W_{\mathrm{joint}}
=
\sum_\alpha \ln W_\alpha.
}
$$

Within a boundary, mutually exclusive macrostate multiplicities add:

$$
\boxed{
\Theta_n
=
\sum_i W_{n,i}.
}
$$

Thus:

> **Compatible possibilities multiply.**

> **Mutually exclusive alternatives add.**

# Enclosing Compatibility and Possibility

## \(\mathcal E_{n+1|n,\alpha,i}\) — Enclosing compatibility fiber

For local peer \(\alpha\) classified as state \(i\),

$$
\boxed{
\mathcal E_{n+1|n,\alpha,i}
}
$$

is the set of enclosing formal microstates compatible with that local
classification.

## \(\Theta_{n+1|n,\alpha,i}\) — Compatible enclosing multiplicity

$$
\boxed{
\Theta_{n+1|n,\alpha,i}
=
\left|
\mathcal E_{n+1|n,\alpha,i}
\right|.
}
$$

This is the number of enclosing realizations compatible with the specified
local state.

Do not confuse this conditioned quantity with the total local multiplicity

$$
\Theta_n.
$$

## \(K_{n+1|n,\alpha,i}\) — Compatible enclosing extension per local possibility

Define

$$
\boxed{
K_{n+1|n,\alpha,i}
=
\frac{
\Theta_{n+1|n,\alpha,i}
}{
W_{n,\alpha,i}
}.
}
$$

This gives the compatible enclosing extension multiplicity per local
possibility.

## \(P_{n,\alpha,i}\) — Possibility coordinate

Possibility is

$$
\boxed{
P_{n,\alpha,i}
=
\ln K_{n+1|n,\alpha,i}.
}
$$

It is a logarithmic across-boundary count relation.

It is not probability.

It is not energy.

## \(\Delta P_{n,\alpha,i\rightarrow k}\) — Directional possibility

$$
\boxed{
\Delta P_{n,\alpha,i\rightarrow k}
=
P_{n,\alpha,k}
-
P_{n,\alpha,i}.
}
$$

Equivalently,

$$
\boxed{
\Delta P_{n,\alpha,i\rightarrow k}
=
\ln
\left(
\frac{
K_{n+1|n,\alpha,k}
}{
K_{n+1|n,\alpha,i}
}
\right).
}
$$

If

$$
K_{n+1|n,\alpha,k}
=
K_{n+1|n,\alpha,i},
$$

then

$$
\boxed{
\Delta P=0.
}
$$

Large absolute possibility does not by itself create direction.

Unequal enclosing compatibility does.

[Possibility →](possibility.qmd)

# Occurrence and Occupancy

## \(\mu_n^{(r)}\) — Realized formal microstate

$$
\boxed{
\mu_n^{(r)}
\in
\mathfrak M_n
}
$$

denotes one realized formal microstate.

If

$$
\pi_n\left(\mu_n^{(r)}\right)=i,
$$

that realization contributes one occurrence associated with macrostate \(i\).

## \(\nu_{n,i}\) — State occurrence count

$$
\boxed{
\nu_{n,i}
}
$$

is the number of realized formal microstate occurrences classified as
macrostate \(i\) within a specified finite realization domain.

Occurrence is **realized instance count**.

## \(\tau_{n,i}\) — Logarithmic occurrence coordinate

For

$$
\nu_{n,i}>0,
$$

define

$$
\boxed{
\tau_{n,i}
=
\ln\nu_{n,i}.
}
$$

This is not physical time.

## \(\Delta\tau_{n,i\rightarrow k}\) — State occurrence difference

$$
\boxed{
\Delta\tau_{n,i\rightarrow k}
=
\tau_{n,k}-\tau_{n,i}
=
\ln
\left(
\frac{\nu_{n,k}}{\nu_{n,i}}
\right).
}
$$

## \(c_{n,i}\) — Occupancy

$$
\boxed{
c_{n,i}
}
$$

is the realized occupancy associated with macrostate \(i\).

Occupancy describes realized structure across the macrostate landscape.

It is not the same as the number of occurrences.

## \(G_{n,i}\) — Logarithmic occupancy coordinate

For positive occupancy,

$$
\boxed{
G_{n,i}
=
\ln c_{n,i}.
}
$$

This \(G\) is **not Gibbs free energy**.

## \(\Delta G_{n,i\rightarrow k}\) — Occupancy difference

$$
\boxed{
\Delta G_{n,i\rightarrow k}
=
G_{n,k}-G_{n,i}
=
\ln
\left(
\frac{c_{n,k}}{c_{n,i}}
\right).
}
$$

## \(i_n^*\) — Structural macrostate

The structural macrostate is the macrostate of maximum occupancy:

$$
\boxed{
i_n^*
=
\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{i\in\mathcal M_n}
c_{n,i}.
}
$$

# Three Count Types That Must Not Be Confused

The three primary local counts are

$$
\boxed{
W_{n,i}
=
\text{possible count},
}
$$

$$
\boxed{
\nu_{n,i}
=
\text{realized occurrence count},
}
$$

and

$$
\boxed{
c_{n,i}
=
\text{realized occupancy}.
}
$$

Their logarithmic coordinates are

$$
\boxed{
S_{n,i},
\qquad
\tau_{n,i},
\qquad
G_{n,i}.
}
$$

Thus:

> **Multiplicity asks what can occur.**

> **Occurrence asks what happens.**

> **Occupancy asks what realized structure is expressed.**

[Occupancy and Occurrence →](occupancy-occurrence.qmd)

# Proportional Occurrence Realization

R<sup>2</sup>D postulates, under the specified proportional-realization
conditions,

$$
\boxed{
\frac{\nu_{n,k}}{\nu_{n,i}}
\approx
\frac{W_{n,k}}{W_{n,i}}.
}
$$

Equivalently,

$$
\boxed{
\Delta\tau_{n,i\rightarrow k}
\approx
\Delta S_{n,i\rightarrow k}.
}
$$

This does not mean

$$
\nu_{n,i}=W_{n,i}.
$$

The relation is between relative structures.

# Distinguishability

## \(\lambda_{n,i\rightarrow k}\) — Readable distinguishability interval

$$
\boxed{
\lambda_{n,i\rightarrow k}
}
$$

is the oriented readable distinction between macrostates \(i\) and \(k\).

It reverses sign under reversal:

$$
\boxed{
\lambda_{n,k\rightarrow i}
=
-
\lambda_{n,i\rightarrow k}.
}
$$

At the primitive level, \(\lambda\) is not necessarily spatial length,
displacement, energy, or time.

Those are possible later physical reads.

# Constraint

## \(C_{n+1}\) — Total enclosing constraint

$$
\boxed{
C_{n+1}\geq0
}
$$

is the total constraint associated with the enclosing occurrence.

It can be decomposed as

$$
\boxed{
C_{n+1}
=
C_{n+1}^{\mathrm{out}}
+
C_{n+1}^{\Phi}.
}
$$

## \(C_{n+1}^{\mathrm{out}}\) — Productive/output constraint

$$
\boxed{
C_{n+1}^{\mathrm{out}}
}
$$

is the component that defines local retention and remains readable as
productive distinguishable output.

## \(C_{n+1}^{\Phi}\) — Background-associated constraint

$$
\boxed{
C_{n+1}^{\Phi}
}
$$

is the background-associated or dissipative component.

It contributes to the total enclosing constrained read but does not enter
local retention.

# Retention

## \(\Delta R_{n,i\rightarrow k}\) — Local retention

For readable transition

$$
i\rightarrow k,
$$

retention is

$$
\boxed{
\Delta R_{n,i\rightarrow k}
=
C_{n+1}^{\mathrm{out}}
\lambda_{n,i\rightarrow k}.
}
$$

Because constraint is nonnegative and distinguishability is oriented,

$$
\boxed{
\Delta R_{n,k\rightarrow i}
=
-
\Delta R_{n,i\rightarrow k}
}
$$

when the same productive constraint applies.

[Constraint and Retention →](constraint-retention.qmd)

# Asymmetry

## \(\Delta A_{n,i\rightarrow k}\) — Net local asymmetry

Local asymmetry is the directional possibility remaining after retention:

$$
\boxed{
\Delta A_{n,i\rightarrow k}
=
\Delta P_{n,i\rightarrow k}
-
\Delta R_{n,i\rightarrow k}.
}
$$

It is not an additional independent primitive cause.

It is the difference between possibility and retention.

## Occupancy-realization relation

R<sup>2</sup>D postulates

$$
\boxed{
\Delta G_{n,i\rightarrow k}
=
\Delta\tau_{n,i\rightarrow k}
+
\Delta A_{n,i\rightarrow k}.
}
$$

Under proportional occurrence realization,

$$
\boxed{
\Delta G
\approx
\Delta S+\Delta P-\Delta R.
}
$$

[Asymmetry →](asymmetry.qmd)

# Stall

The stall condition is

$$
\boxed{
\Delta P
=
\Delta R.
}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\boxed{
\Delta A=0.
}
$$

Stall does not require

$$
\Delta P=0.
$$

It means directional possibility is completely retained.

# Return and Closure

## \(\mathcal R_n\) — Macrostate return

A finite readable path

$$
\mathcal R_n:
i_0
\rightarrow
i_1
\rightarrow
\cdots
\rightarrow
i_m
$$

is a return when

$$
\boxed{
i_m=i_0.
}
$$

Return is defined entirely by local path completion.

## \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\) — Closure

A local return is a closure relative to \(B_{n+1}\) when it is compatible with
an enclosing occurrence.

For peer \(\alpha\),

$$
\boxed{
\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}.
}
$$

For a minimal closure,

$$
\boxed{
\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}:
i\rightarrow k\rightarrow i.
}
$$

Thus:

> **Return = local path completion.**

> **Closure = local return compatible with an enclosing occurrence.**

[Closure →](closure.qmd)

# Closure-Level Quantities

## Native multiplicity closure

Around a genuine closed state path,

$$
\boxed{
\Delta S_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}=0.
}
$$

## Closure possibility

$$
\boxed{
\Delta P_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}
=
\sum_{\chi\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}}
\Delta P_{n,\alpha,\chi}.
}
$$

## Closure retention

$$
\boxed{
\Delta R_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}
=
\sum_{\chi\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}}
\Delta R_{n,\alpha,\chi}.
}
$$

## Closure asymmetry

$$
\boxed{
\Delta A_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}
=
\Delta P_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}
-
\Delta R_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}.
}
$$

Complete retention gives

$$
\boxed{
\Delta A_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}=0.
}
$$

The local multiplicity can close exactly while closure asymmetry remains
nonzero.

# Opposed-Leg Occurrence Counts

## \(\nu_{n,\alpha,H}\)

$$
\boxed{
\nu_{n,\alpha,H}
}
$$

counts completed realizations of oriented closure leg \(H\).

## \(\nu_{n,\alpha,L}\)

$$
\boxed{
\nu_{n,\alpha,L}
}
$$

counts completed realizations of the opposed leg \(L\).

These are complete-path occurrence counts.

They are not sums of the individual state occurrence counts.

# Directional Occurrence-Count Efficiency

## \(\eta_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}\)

Choose the orientation so that

$$
0<
\eta_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}
\leq1.
$$

Then

$$
\boxed{
\eta_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}
=
\frac{
\nu_{n,\alpha,L}
}{
\nu_{n,\alpha,H}
}.
}
$$

Reciprocal realization:

$$
\boxed{
\eta=1.
}
$$

Nonreciprocal realization:

$$
\boxed{
0<\eta<1.
}
$$

# Opposed-Leg Nonreciprocity

## \(\Delta\tau_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}\)

The logarithmic opposed-leg occurrence difference is

$$
\boxed{
\Delta\tau_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}
=
\ln
\eta_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}.
}
$$

## \(L_{\tau,n,\alpha,\mathcal C}\) — Occurrence-count loss

Define

$$
\boxed{
L_{\tau,n,\alpha,\mathcal C}
=
-\Delta\tau_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}
=
-\ln\eta_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}.
}
$$

Equivalently,

$$
\boxed{
L_{\tau,n,\alpha,\mathcal C}
=
\ln
\left(
\frac{
\nu_{n,\alpha,H}
}{
\nu_{n,\alpha,L}
}
\right).
}
$$

Thus,

$$
\boxed{
L_\tau\geq0.
}
$$

"Loss" means directional nonreciprocity.

It does not mean destruction of count.

# Recurrence

## \(\mathcal D_R\) — Recurrence-comparison domain

$$
\boxed{
\mathcal D_R
}
$$

is a finite count domain in which completed recurrences at adjacent
boundaries are jointly counted.

It is not assumed to be a physical time interval.

## \(N_{\mathcal D_R}(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha})\)

$$
\boxed{
N_{\mathcal D_R}
\left(
\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}
\right)
}
$$

is the number of completed recurrences of representative local closure
\(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\).

## \(N_{\mathcal D_R}(\chi_{n+1})\)

$$
\boxed{
N_{\mathcal D_R}
\left(
\chi_{n+1}
\right)
}
$$

is the number of completed recurrences of the corresponding enclosing
transition class.

[Recurrence →](recurrence.qmd)

# Adjacent Recurrence Ratio

## \(\rho_{n+1|n,\alpha}\)

$$
\boxed{
\rho_{n+1|n,\alpha}
=
\frac{
N_{\mathcal D_R}(\chi_{n+1})
}{
N_{\mathcal D_R}(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha})
}.
}
$$

This is the number of enclosing recurrences per local closure recurrence.

It is dimensionless.

It is not yet a physical rate.

# Three Quantities That Must Never Be Interchanged

These three quantities all involve occurrence or recurrence, but answer
different questions.

### State occurrence difference

$$
\boxed{
\Delta\tau_{n,i\rightarrow k}
=
\ln
\left(
\frac{\nu_{n,k}}{\nu_{n,i}}
\right)
}
$$

asks about relative state occurrences.

### Closure nonreciprocity

$$
\boxed{
L_{\tau,n,\alpha,\mathcal C}
=
\ln
\left(
\frac{\nu_{n,\alpha,H}}
{\nu_{n,\alpha,L}}
\right)
}
$$

asks whether opposed complete closure legs are realized reciprocally.

### Across-boundary recurrence ratio

$$
\boxed{
\rho_{n+1|n,\alpha}
=
\frac{
N_{\mathcal D_R}(\chi_{n+1})
}{
N_{\mathcal D_R}(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha})
}
}
$$

asks how recurrence scales between adjacent boundaries.

Thus:

$$
\boxed{
\Delta\tau
\neq
L_\tau
\neq
\rho.
}
$$

# Enclosing Occurrence

## \(\chi_{n+1}\)

$$
\boxed{
\chi_{n+1}
}
$$

denotes a readable enclosing macrostate transition at \(B_{n+1}\).

## \(\chi_{n+1}^{(r)}\)

$$
\boxed{
\chi_{n+1}^{(r)}
}
$$

denotes one realized occurrence associated with that enclosing transition.

# Compatible Peer Closures

## \(\mathfrak D_{n+1,\chi}\)

$$
\boxed{
\mathfrak D_{n+1,\chi}
}
$$

is the set of joint peer closures compatible with one enclosing occurrence.

Schematically,

$$
\boxed{
\chi_{n+1}^{(r)}
\Longrightarrow
\left(
\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}
\right)_{\alpha\in I_n}
\in
\mathfrak D_{n+1,\chi}.
}
$$

# Causal Realization

The causal relation is

$$
\boxed{
\chi_{n+1}^{(r)}
\Longrightarrow
\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}.
}
$$

This means:

> the enclosing occurrence defines which local closure belongs to its
> compatible realization.

It does **not** mean that the enclosing occurrence physically pushes a local
object downward.

It specifies causal organization.

[The Causal Inversion →](causal-inversion.qmd)

# Recursive Carry

## \(\kappa_n\) — Recursive reclassification

Recursive carry is written

$$
\boxed{
\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}
\xmapsto{\kappa_n}
\chi_{n+1}^{(r)}.
}
$$

This is not a causal arrow.

It means:

> the completed local realization acquires a new count meaning when the
> boundary changes.

Thus the two arrows answer different questions:

$$
\boxed{
\chi_{n+1}^{(r)}
\Longrightarrow
\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}
\qquad
\text{causal realization},
}
$$

while

$$
\boxed{
\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}
\xmapsto{\kappa_n}
\chi_{n+1}^{(r)}
\qquad
\text{recursive reclassification}.
}
$$

[Recursive Carry →](recursive-carry.qmd)

# Background

## \(b_n\) — Background count

$$
\boxed{
b_n>0
}
$$

is a realized nondirectional background count at \(B_n\).

## \(\Phi_n\) — Logarithmic background coordinate

$$
\boxed{
\Phi_n
=
\ln b_n.
}
$$

Background is nondirectional relative to the boundary at which it is
background:

$$
\boxed{
\Delta\Phi_{n,i\rightarrow k}=0.
}
$$

That does not prevent two subordinate backgrounds from becoming
distinguishable relative to an enclosing boundary.

# Enclosing Background Increment

Let

$$
b_{n+1}^{-}
$$

and

$$
b_{n+1}^{+}
$$

denote enclosing background counts before and after one specified realization.

Define

$$
\boxed{
\delta_{\mathcal C}\Phi_{n+1}
=
\ln
\left(
\frac{
b_{n+1}^{+}
}{
b_{n+1}^{-}
}
\right).
}
$$

# The R<sup>2</sup>D Second Law

The Second Law of Recursive Counting is

$$
\boxed{
\delta_{\mathcal C}\Phi_{n+1}
=
L_{\tau,n,\alpha,\mathcal C}
\geq0.
}
$$

This equates two logarithmic count readings at different boundaries.

It does not describe destruction or bottom-up transport of count.

[The R²D Second Law →](second-law.qmd)

# The R<sup>2</sup>D Law

The compact R<sup>2</sup>D law is

$$
\boxed{
\Delta A_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}
=
C_{n+1}
\lambda_{n+1}
\rho_{n+1|n,\alpha}.
}
$$

Equivalently,

$$
\boxed{
\Delta A_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}
N_{\mathcal D_R}
\left(
\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}
\right)
=
C_{n+1}
\lambda_{n+1}
N_{\mathcal D_R}
\left(
\chi_{n+1}
\right).
}
$$

With total constraint explicitly decomposed,

$$
\boxed{
\Delta A_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}
=
\left(
C_{n+1}^{\mathrm{out}}
+
C_{n+1}^{\Phi}
\right)
\lambda_{n+1}
\rho_{n+1|n,\alpha}.
}
$$

This is an invariant relation between boundary-specific recurrence-weighted
readings.

It is not a causal arrow.

[The R²D Law →](r2d-law.qmd)

# Representative Peers

No special representative-peer index is required.

If peers \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are equivalent under the relevant enclosing
compatibility relation, either ordinary peer index may be used.

Their recurrence-weighted readings satisfy

$$
\boxed{
\Delta A_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}
N_{\mathcal D_R}
\left(
\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}
\right)
=
\Delta A_{n,\beta,\mathcal C}
N_{\mathcal D_R}
\left(
\mathcal C_{n,\beta}
\right).
}
$$

For positive recurrence ratios,

$$
\boxed{
\frac{
\Delta A_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}
}{
\rho_{n+1|n,\alpha}
}
=
\frac{
\Delta A_{n,\beta,\mathcal C}
}{
\rho_{n+1|n,\beta}
}.
}
$$

No averaging over peers is implied.

# Accumulated Recursive Scaling

## \(\Lambda_{N|n}\) — Distinguishability scaling

For larger boundary \(B_N\),

$$
\boxed{
\Lambda_{N|n}
=
\ln
\left(
\frac{
|\lambda_N|
}{
|\lambda_n|
}
\right).
}
$$

## \(\Gamma_{N|n}\) — Recurrence scaling

$$
\boxed{
\Gamma_{N|n}
=
\sum_{j=n}^{N-1}
\ln
\rho_{j+1|j}.
}
$$

When one recurrence-comparison domain jointly counts the chain, the adjacent
ratios telescope.

## \(H_{N|n}\) — Accumulated count-geometry imbalance

Define

$$
\boxed{
H_{N|n}
=
\Lambda_{N|n}
-
\Gamma_{N|n}.
}
$$

Equivalently,

$$
\boxed{
H_{N|n}
=
\ln
\left[
\frac{
|\lambda_N|/|\lambda_n|
}{
\displaystyle
\prod_{j=n}^{N-1}
\rho_{j+1|j}
}
\right].
}
$$

\(H\) is not a third primitive coordinate.

It measures the relative accumulated scaling of distinguishability and
recurrence.

[Recursive Counting Across Scale →](recursive-counting.qmd)

# Readability Regimes

A large positive

$$
H
$$

corresponds to a distinguishability-dominant limit:

$$
\boxed{
H\rightarrow+\infty.
}
$$

A large negative value corresponds to a recurrence-dominant limit:

$$
\boxed{
H\rightarrow-\infty.
}
$$

At finite relative geometry,

$$
\boxed{
|H|<\infty,
}
$$

both relations may remain jointly readable if neither has crossed a
resolution limit.

A mathematical limit alone does not define a horizon.

A readability horizon additionally requires one relation to become
unresolvable while the other remains readable.

# Recursive Limits

## \(B_\alpha\) — Smallest realized boundary

$$
\boxed{
B_\alpha
}
$$

is the smallest realized count boundary in the present formalism.

It supplies primitive distinguishable recurrence without requiring a realized
\(B_{\alpha-1}\).

## \(B_\omega\) — Largest presently realized boundary

$$
\boxed{
B_\omega
}
$$

is the largest presently realized count boundary.

## \(\mathcal O_\omega\) — Terminal open path

The presently open path is

$$
\boxed{
\mathcal O_\omega:
i_{\omega,0}
\rightarrow
\cdots
\rightarrow
i_{\omega,m},
\qquad
i_{\omega,m}\neq i_{\omega,0}.
}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\boxed{
\mathcal O_\omega
\neq
\mathcal C_\omega.
}
$$

The terminal postulate therefore does not assume a completed enclosing
\(B_{\omega+1}\).

## \(\Delta A_{\omega,\mathcal O}\) — Terminal unresolved asymmetry

$$
\boxed{
\Delta A_{\omega,\mathcal O}
}
$$

denotes the unresolved directional asymmetry of the terminal open path.

Unlike ordinary local asymmetry, it is not defined from a still larger
realized possibility-retention relation.

# Common Symbol Confusions

## \(P\neq p\)

$$
P
$$

is R<sup>2</sup>D possibility: logarithmic compatible enclosing extension.

$$
p
$$

is probability: a normalized count read.

They are not the same quantity.

## \(G\neq\) Gibbs free energy

Primitive

$$
G_{n,i}
=
\ln c_{n,i}
$$

is the logarithmic occupancy coordinate.

Conventional Gibbs free energy is a later thermodynamic quantity.

## \(\tau\neq t\)

$$
\tau
=
\ln\nu
$$

is a logarithmic occurrence coordinate.

It is not elapsed time.

## \(\lambda\neq\) primitive length

$$
\lambda
$$

is readable distinguishability.

A physical length or displacement may later read it in a specified mapping.

## \(C\neq\) primitive force

$$
C
$$

is enclosing constraint.

Force can be one physical mechanical read.

## \(S=\ln W\) is dimensionless first

Primitive

$$
S
=
\ln W
$$

is logarithmic multiplicity.

Thermodynamic entropy appears only after physical dimensionalization.

## \(\rho\neq\eta\)

$$
\rho
$$

compares recurrence across boundaries.

$$
\eta
$$

compares occurrence efficiency between opposed legs of one local closure.

They answer different questions.

## \(\Delta A\neq L_\tau\)

$$
\Delta A
$$

describes directional asymmetry.

$$
L_\tau
$$

describes occurrence nonreciprocity.

Directionality is not identical to irreversibility.

# Count-Type Summary

| Relation | State-defined | Transition-defined | Closure / across-boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Native multiplicity | \(W_{n,i},\,S_{n,i}\) | \(\Delta S_{n,i\rightarrow k}\) | \(\Delta S_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}=0\) |
| Enclosing possibility | \(P_{n,\alpha,i}\) | \(\Delta P_{n,\alpha,i\rightarrow k}\) | \(\Delta P_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}\) |
| State occurrence | \(\nu_{n,i},\,\tau_{n,i}\) | \(\Delta\tau_{n,i\rightarrow k}\) | — |
| Occupancy | \(c_{n,i},\,G_{n,i}\) | \(\Delta G_{n,i\rightarrow k}\) | — |
| Distinguishability | — | \(\lambda_{n,i\rightarrow k}\) | \(\lambda_{n+1}\) in enclosing read |
| Retention | — | \(\Delta R_{n,i\rightarrow k}\) | \(\Delta R_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}\) |
| Asymmetry | — | \(\Delta A_{n,i\rightarrow k}\) | \(\Delta A_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}\) |
| Closure recurrence | — | — | \(N_{\mathcal D_R}(\mathcal C),\,\rho\) |
| Complete-leg realization | — | — | \(\nu_H,\,\nu_L\) |
| Leg nonreciprocity | — | — | \(\eta,\,\Delta\tau_{\mathcal C},\,L_\tau\) |
| Background | \(b_n,\,\Phi_n\) | enclosing background comparison | \(\delta_{\mathcal C}\Phi_{n+1}\) |

# Primitive Definitions Versus Physical Reads

The symbols on this page are primitive R<sup>2</sup>D quantities.

Later physical mappings may assign familiar scientific coordinates to them.

Examples include:

$$
\ln W
\xrightarrow{\text{thermodynamic read}}
\text{entropy},
$$

$$
C^{\mathrm{out}}\lambda
\xrightarrow{\text{mechanical read}}
\text{work-like quantity},
$$

$$
\rho
\xrightarrow{\text{temporal read}}
\text{relative physical rate},
$$

and

$$
\lambda
\xrightarrow{\text{geometric read}}
\text{spatial distinction}.
$$

These are mappings.

They are not primitive definitions.

[From Count to Physical Science →](from-count-to-physics.qmd)

# The Core Architecture in Compact Form

The definitions can be summarized as one sequence:

$$
\boxed{
B_n
\rightarrow
\mathfrak M_n
\xrightarrow{\pi_n}
\mathcal M_n
\rightarrow
W_{n,i}
\rightarrow
S_{n,i}
}
$$

followed by realization:

$$
\boxed{
W
\rightarrow
\nu
\rightarrow
c
}
$$

with enclosing organization:

$$
\boxed{
\Theta_{n+1|n}
\rightarrow
P
\rightarrow
\Delta P
}
$$

and retention:

$$
\boxed{
C^{\mathrm{out}}
\lambda
\rightarrow
\Delta R
}
$$

giving

$$
\boxed{
\Delta A
=
\Delta P-\Delta R.
}
$$

Closure gives

$$
\boxed{
\mathcal C_n,
}
$$

recurrence gives

$$
\boxed{
\rho_{n+1|n},
}
$$

and adjacent boundaries are related by

$$
\boxed{
\Delta A_{n,\alpha,\mathcal C}
=
C_{n+1}
\lambda_{n+1}
\rho_{n+1|n,\alpha}.
}
$$

Nonreciprocal local realization gives

$$
\boxed{
L_{\tau,n,\alpha,\mathcal C}
=
\delta_{\mathcal C}\Phi_{n+1}.
}
$$

And changing the boundary gives recursive reclassification:

$$
\boxed{
\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}
\xmapsto{\kappa_n}
\chi_{n+1}^{(r)}.
}
$$

# The Five Distinctions to Remember

If only five things are retained from this reference page, they should be:

> **1. Statehood is boundary relative.**

> **2. Multiplicity, occurrence, and occupancy are different count types.**

> **3. Possibility comes from enclosing compatibility; retention comes from
> constraint acting across distinguishability.**

> **4. Closure, directionality, recurrence, and irreversibility are different
> relations.**

> **5. Recursive carry changes count meaning; it is not reverse causation.**

Everything else in the R<sup>2</sup>D formalism is built by keeping those
distinctions intact.
